# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.

  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
- Reading:
  - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

> # Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side
> ## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
> - Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
> - Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.
> ## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
> Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
> 2 branches per separator.
> - Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
> - Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
> - Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
> - Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.
> ## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
> - At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
> - Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
> - m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.
> ## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
> - m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
> - That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
> - Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
> - Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
> - m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
> - Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
> - The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
> - Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
> - Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
> - The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
> - Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
> - Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.
> ## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
> - RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
> - Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
>   - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
>   - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
>   - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
>   - Cut off again: undecided.
> ## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
> - Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
> - Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
> - Reading:
>   - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
>   - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Resume: crypto @ claude/fastest-grobner-base-algorithm-u74ipw (Gröbner solver shootout, 2026-11-16)

## Goal
User (2026-11-16, via workflow): controlled comparison of Gröbner/algebraic solvers on Weil-descended
Semaev decomposition systems over GF(2^n), m = 3 and m = 4: msolve F4, Magma F4 (UNAVAILABLE unless a
licensed binary is reachable; never faked), CryptoMiniSat with native XOR, fixed-schedule F4 replay
(learn once, apply). Per system: degree reached, largest matrix, wall, peak RSS; cost per relation vs
matched Pollard rho in the AGENTS.md §5a band (0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE).

## Lead / hypothesis
No directional hypothesis is decisive. Prior lab work is all [pcc:unverified] (m4gb ladder, gb_cas_comparison,
sat_pdp_pricing_band, prime-field trace F4). Trace/learn_apply has never been measured on binary m = 3/4.

## Spec
research/groebner_solver_shootout_20261116/PROTOCOL.md + protocol.json (experiment.protocol/v1,
GB-SOLVER-SHOOTOUT-20261116, frozen 2026-11-16T16:55:09Z, protocol_sha256
116b33f754becbd9d7e76cbd80bfff8e323cb79ab0ee0c57481c0616d3d9bfee). grid.tsv (15 cell-variants),
analyze.py (sha256 0b0eee39...7929, frozen before data). Seeds derive from the protocol hash.
Instruments: msolve 0.6.5-1build2 (sha256 c2722288...59fa), cryptominisat5 5.11.15 (00db7e59...7207),
groebner_compare/{semaev,external_worker,semaev_verifier,runner,certificate}.py (hashes in
protocol.json execution.placement.harness_files_sha256_at_freeze).

## State
- groebner_compare Semaev generator, msolve/CMS/Magma adapters, verifier, 21 unit tests: written, UNCOMMITTED.
- Protocol frozen; NOT launched. No main-run data. Preflight (one planted seed-1 instance per cell,
  shared container, development only): preflight/timings.tsv.
- Arms UNAVAILABLE at freeze: magma-f4 (no binary/licence), trace-f4 and julia-f4-warm (no Julia; proxy
  403 on julialang-s3; per-target supports differ).

## Next steps
1. Commit and push study + groebner_compare changes (record source revision; freeze.commit 66d8635 is the parent).
2. Implement prerequisites P1-P6 (PROTOCOL.md "Prerequisites") without changing the design; pin hashes.
3. Fix run gates (P7): valid AWS identity, CHECKPOINT_UPLOAD_TOKEN, gh token, benchrec gate (2 pre-existing failing
   records), Conductor; owner approval of USD 15 ceiling.
4. experiment-director writes the isolab-eks command-Job card; executor-mechanical runs it; director assesses.
5. analyze.py phase 1 blind, then phase 2 with key; research-visuals report; bench.record/v1.

## Runs in flight
None.

## Stop and success conditions
Fixed N (15 cells x (1 warm-up + 5 planted + 40 natural) x available arms); 300 CPU-s / 8 GiB per call;
USD 15, 24 vCPU concurrent. Success = all rows certified and reported per the frozen decision rule,
including UNAVAILABLE and censored arms; every rho gap reported as distance remaining. Clocks from command
Jobs are diagnostic tier only (no L2 admission).

## Open questions
- Whether an L2-admitted path for external solvers (ecbench method) should be a v2 protocol.
- Whether to provision Julia (network policy) or build a native fixed-schedule replay for trace-f4 (amendment).

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
- Reading:
  - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

> # Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side
> ## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
> - Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
> - Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.
> ## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
> Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
> 2 branches per separator.
> - Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
> - Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
> - Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
> - Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.
> ## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
> - At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
> - Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
> - m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.
> ## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
> - m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
> - That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
> - Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
> - Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
> - m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
> - Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
> - The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
> - Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
> - Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
> - The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
> - Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
> - Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.
> ## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
> - RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
> - Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
>   - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
>   - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
>   - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
>   - Cut off again: undecided.
> ## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
> - Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
> - Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
> - Reading:

>   - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Resume: crypto @ claude/fastest-grobner-base-algorithm-u74ipw (Gröbner solver shootout, 2026-11-16)

## Goal
User (2026-11-16, via workflow): controlled comparison of Gröbner/algebraic solvers on Weil-descended
Semaev decomposition systems over GF(2^n), m = 3 and m = 4: msolve F4, Magma F4 (UNAVAILABLE unless a
licensed binary is reachable; never faked), CryptoMiniSat with native XOR, fixed-schedule F4 replay
(learn once, apply). Per system: degree reached, largest matrix, wall, peak RSS; cost per relation vs
matched Pollard rho in the AGENTS.md §5a band (0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE).

## Lead / hypothesis
No directional hypothesis is decisive. Prior lab work is all [pcc:unverified] (m4gb ladder, gb_cas_comparison,
sat_pdp_pricing_band, prime-field trace F4). Trace/learn_apply has never been measured on binary m = 3/4.

## Spec
research/groebner_solver_shootout_20261116/PROTOCOL.md + protocol.json (experiment.protocol/v1,
GB-SOLVER-SHOOTOUT-20261116, frozen 2026-11-16T16:55:09Z, protocol_sha256
116b33f754becbd9d7e76cbd80bfff8e323cb79ab0ee0c57481c0616d3d9bfee). grid.tsv (15 cell-variants),
analyze.py (sha256 0b0eee39...7929, frozen before data). Seeds derive from the protocol hash.
Instruments: msolve 0.6.5-1build2 (sha256 c2722288...59fa), cryptominisat5 5.11.15 (00db7e59...7207),
groebner_compare/{semaev,external_worker,semaev_verifier,runner,certificate}.py (hashes in
protocol.json execution.placement.harness_files_sha256_at_freeze).

## State
- groebner_compare Semaev generator, msolve/CMS/Magma adapters, verifier, 21 unit tests: written, UNCOMMITTED.
- Protocol frozen; NOT launched. No main-run data. Preflight (one planted seed-1 instance per cell,
  shared container, development only): preflight/timings.tsv.
- Arms UNAVAILABLE at freeze: magma-f4 (no binary/licence), trace-f4 and julia-f4-warm (no Julia; proxy
  403 on julialang-s3; per-target supports differ).

## Next steps
1. Commit and push study + groebner_compare changes (record source revision; freeze.commit 66d8635 is the parent).
2. Implement prerequisites P1-P6 (PROTOCOL.md "Prerequisites") without changing the design; pin hashes.
3. Fix run gates (P7): valid AWS identity, CHECKPOINT_UPLOAD_TOKEN, gh token, benchrec gate (2 pre-existing failing
   records), Conductor; owner approval of USD 15 ceiling.
4. experiment-director writes the isolab-eks command-Job card; executor-mechanical runs it; director assesses.
5. analyze.py phase 1 blind, then phase 2 with key; research-visuals report; bench.record/v1.

## Runs in flight
None.

## Stop and success conditions
Fixed N (15 cells x (1 warm-up + 5 planted + 40 natural) x available arms); 300 CPU-s / 8 GiB per call;
USD 15, 24 vCPU concurrent. Success = all rows certified and reported per the frozen decision rule,
including UNAVAILABLE and censored arms; every rho gap reported as distance remaining. Clocks from command
Jobs are diagnostic tier only (no L2 admission).

## Open questions
- Whether an L2-admitted path for external solvers (ecbench method) should be a v2 protocol.
- Whether to provision Julia (network policy) or build a native fixed-schedule replay for trace-f4 (amendment).

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
- Reading:
  - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.

  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

Explains cost only, claims no speedup. None yet.

Stop if checkpoint push fails or the CPU lock cannot be obtained; report that plainly.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

first-witness correctness screens; their timing is not yet known.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
- Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
- Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.

## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
- RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
- Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
  - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
  - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
  - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
  - Cut off again: undecided.

## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
- Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
- Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
- Reading:
  - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
  - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

> # Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side
> ## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
> - Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
> - Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.
> ## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
> Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
> 2 branches per separator.
> - Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
> - Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
> - Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
> - Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.
> ## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
> - At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
> - Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
> - m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.
> ## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
> - m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
> - That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
> - Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
> - Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
> - m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
> - Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
> - The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
> - Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
> - Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.
> ## Round 6 (2026-11-04): local long run of the P2 cell m5 t4 (written before the run)
> - The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
> - Locally: T at m5 t4 (round 3; cut off at 2,400 s while reducing degree 9, memory not exhausted), rerun alone with TLIMIT = 18,000 s and VLIMIT = 14.5 GiB.
> - Registered reading (from round 3): if the run completes with D = 9 then E(5) = 5 ≤ 5 and P2 holds at m = 5; D ≥ 10 means P2 fails at m = 5; another cut-off is still undecided.
> ## Round 7d: decisive Riemann–Roch cell (written before the run)
> - RR at m5 t4 (round7_rr/genrr.sing, input in scratchpad rr/logs/m5_t4_k0_RR.ms), alone on the host after the memory-lean F4 run exits: 13 GiB cap, 10,800 s.
> - Reading, from round7_rr's kill criterion:
>   - D_RR ≤ 8 (below T's ≥ 9) with a finished run: RR beats T in D at m = 5.
>   - Improvement only if the widest matrix is also below T's (≥ 999,374 cut off).
>   - D_RR ≥ 9 means no gain at m = 5.
>   - Cut off again: undecided.
> ## Round 7e: E1Q at m4 t5 (written before the run)
> - Edwards 2-torsion-quotient tree, input round7_edwards m4_t5_E1Q.ms (sha256 5592ad57…f099).
> - Runs alone after RR m5 t4 exits, with a 13 GiB cap and 7,200 s.
> - Reading:
>   - D_E1Q(4,5) finishes ≤ 6 (T and E1 are ≥ 7 there): the excess stays at least 1 below T at m = 4 as t grows.
>   - D = 7: the quotient's gain at m = 4 vanishes at t = 5.

# Resume: crypto @ claude/fastest-grobner-base-algorithm-u74ipw (Gröbner solver shootout, 2026-11-16)

## Goal
User (2026-11-16, via workflow): controlled comparison of Gröbner/algebraic solvers on Weil-descended
Semaev decomposition systems over GF(2^n), m = 3 and m = 4: msolve F4, Magma F4 (UNAVAILABLE unless a
licensed binary is reachable; never faked), CryptoMiniSat with native XOR, fixed-schedule F4 replay
(learn once, apply). Per system: degree reached, largest matrix, wall, peak RSS; cost per relation vs
matched Pollard rho in the AGENTS.md §5a band (0 / 0.1 / 1 GAE).

## Lead / hypothesis
No directional hypothesis is decisive. Prior lab work is all [pcc:unverified] (m4gb ladder, gb_cas_comparison,
sat_pdp_pricing_band, prime-field trace F4). Trace/learn_apply has never been measured on binary m = 3/4.

## Spec
research/groebner_solver_shootout_20261116/PROTOCOL.md + protocol.json (experiment.protocol/v1,
GB-SOLVER-SHOOTOUT-20261116, frozen 2026-11-16T16:55:09Z, protocol_sha256
116b33f754becbd9d7e76cbd80bfff8e323cb79ab0ee0c57481c0616d3d9bfee). grid.tsv (15 cell-variants),
analyze.py (sha256 0b0eee39...7929, frozen before data). Seeds derive from the protocol hash.
Instruments: msolve 0.6.5-1build2 (sha256 c2722288...59fa), cryptominisat5 5.11.15 (00db7e59...7207),
groebner_compare/{semaev,external_worker,semaev_verifier,runner,certificate}.py (hashes in
protocol.json execution.placement.harness_files_sha256_at_freeze).

## State
- groebner_compare Semaev generator, msolve/CMS/Magma adapters, verifier, 21 unit tests: written, UNCOMMITTED.
- Protocol frozen; NOT launched. No main-run data. Preflight (one planted seed-1 instance per cell,
  shared container, development only): preflight/timings.tsv.
- Arms UNAVAILABLE at freeze: magma-f4 (no binary/licence), trace-f4 and julia-f4-warm (no Julia; proxy
  403 on julialang-s3; per-target supports differ).

## Next steps
1. Commit and push study + groebner_compare changes (record source revision; freeze.commit 66d8635 is the parent).
2. Implement prerequisites P1-P6 (PROTOCOL.md "Prerequisites") without changing the design; pin hashes.
3. Fix run gates (P7): valid AWS identity, CHECKPOINT_UPLOAD_TOKEN, gh token, benchrec gate (2 pre-existing failing
   records), Conductor; owner approval of USD 15 ceiling.
4. experiment-director writes the isolab-eks command-Job card; executor-mechanical runs it; director assesses.
5. analyze.py phase 1 blind, then phase 2 with key; research-visuals report; bench.record/v1.

## Runs in flight
None.

## Stop and success conditions
Fixed N (15 cells x (1 warm-up + 5 planted + 40 natural) x available arms); 300 CPU-s / 8 GiB per call;
USD 15, 24 vCPU concurrent. Success = all rows certified and reported per the frozen decision rule,
including UNAVAILABLE and censored arms; every rho gap reported as distance remaining. Clocks from command
Jobs are diagnostic tier only (no L2 admission).

## Open questions
- Whether an L2-admitted path for external solvers (ecbench method) should be a v2 protocol.
- Whether to provision Julia (network policy) or build a native fixed-schedule replay for trace-f4 (amendment).

# Round 5 (2026-11-04, written before any round-5 run): solver side

## Derived first (no runs; awk on recorded logs)
- Cost model with LA exponent ω from 1.0 to 2.0: beating rho at 2^256 needs ω ≤ ~1.3 and β = 0.
- Effective sparse-LA exponent of the recorded msolve matrices: 2.41–2.72. Sparsity does not get there.

## Test H: character-hybrid on the separators
Branch on the quadratic character of each separator, adding X_c = n_j·z_c² with n_j ∈ {1, a non-square}:
2 branches per separator.
- Cells: T at m3 t4 (D = 6, 3.7 s), m3 t5 (D = 6, 512 s) and m4 t4 (D = 7, 697 s). Run the planted (true) branch and one false branch each.
- Prediction (Elekes–Szabó reading): D_H = D_T in the true branch (no degree drop), and the false branch costs about the same time.
- Win condition: D drops by ≥ 1 per guessed bit, or total time over all branches < T's time.
- Runs: msolve 1 thread, 1800 s cap, 6 GiB.

## Round 5, test H outcome (recorded before test L)
- At m3 t4, Htrue and Hfalse match T exactly (D = 6, widest 7,077), each with quotient dimension 6 (z ↦ −z).
- Reason: over F̄_p every X is c·z²; F_p-rationality is not a low-degree algebraic constraint.
- m3 t5 was stopped at 42 s, still on T's matrices; m4 t4 was not run.

## Test L (fat-leaf tree, written before any L run)
- m = 4 as one triple (S4sym in e1, e2, e3 with output X1, degree-3 remainder chain) plus one leaf (Kummer chain), root S3(X1, x4, xR).
- That is 1 separator against T's 2 separators (X1, X2) with a symmetric root.
- Prediction (excess ∝ number of separators): D_L(4,4) ≤ 6 < D_T = 7.
- Falsified if D_L ≥ 7. Cells: m4 at t4 and t5, k0.

## Test Y (function coupling, written before any Y run)
- m = 3, first cherry by chord: per-root Kummer chains for w1 and w2; y1, y2 with y_i² = f(g·w_i); slope lam with lam·(x2 − x1) = y2 − y1; X1 = lam² − x1 − x2.
- Then the x-only root S3(X1, g·w3, xR) with leaf 3 on a Kummer chain.
- The coupling is a function of the inputs (no 2-to-2 correspondence). Solutions are not quotiented: ordered pair × signs.
- Prediction: D_Y ≥ D_T (6 at t = 4), since lost symmetry and degree-3 curve equations offset the determinism. Win condition: D_Y ≤ 5 at t = 4 or 5.
- Cells: m3 at t4 and t5, k0.

- The big host is blocked: AWS STS rejects the keys, the lab routes run only ecbench specs (≤ 3,600 s), and no other route is authorized.
